featuresUsed: Profile-specific retail game and cgame modules, selected map collision/render assets, FnQ3/FnQL glx/vk/rtx renderer modules and dynamic-light shadow atlas allocation.

Shared OpenAL spatial backend with inverse_clamped distance model, enabled occlusion, EFX eaxreverb + lowpass filtering and engine-owned audio-zone sidecars (garden1: 512 zones; fakkhouse: 343 zones).
Shared music stream queue (4 buffers), registered profile samples, alpha foliage/sprites and cinematic views.
limits: Bounded startup and first-snapshot proof only: no campaign navigation, player input, saves, demos or bidirectional network interoperability in these nine probes.
Audio remained muted by the private desktop focus policy; this is diagnostics evidence, not an auditory judgement.
Host OpenAL32.dll / Generic Software Compatibility Mode exposes EFX but no OpenAL Soft extensions: HRTF, output limiter status, highpass and bandpass filter capability were unavailable.
The rtx modules ran the default raster path with ray tracing disabled; no accelerated-ray-tracing claim.
Static-light sidecar or per-pixel output use was not logged by these probes; no additional feature claim beyond actual diagnostics.

Initial cinematic captures were unsynchronised; character absence on Alice vk/rtx was not present after skipcinematic. Three later views all display Alice and the same garden world. F.A.K.K.2 vk/rtx bloom is visibly stronger than glx; no exhaustive renderer parity claim.
unrelatedIssues: Both profiles reported conflicting initial fraglimit/cheats values and reused model images with mixed registration flags. F.A.K.K.2 also reported missing sound/misc/null.wav.
The host OpenAL runtime lacks the OpenAL Soft extensions needed to exercise HRTF and the full spatial-filter feature set.

ritual.scope: Nonfatal diagnostic audit of final GLx all-map startup sweep: Alice 36 and F.A.K.K.2 30. No source edits or additional runtime runs during this audit.

findings.name: hedge2 CM_GridPlane unresolvable
findings.facts: The current log has exactly ten warnings and reaches the first snapshot and normal map-load completion. The prior Alice map record already measured exactly ten under all tested patch rules and both precisions, and names the same retail Com_Printf diagnostic at alice.exe 0x004335ac. This is not evidence of a new collision regression.
findings.limits: A successful startup and a historical matching warning do not establish traversal collision correctness for every hedge2 surface.

findings.name: Alice optional startup cfg files absent
findings.facts: Each Alice map prints one could-not-exec line for each of the three cfg names. None of the ten mounted legitimate retail paks contains those root names; default.cfg is present. Both retail Ritual engines queue this configuration sequence; F.A.K.K.2 ships these files and its 30 runs print none of the messages.
findings.limits: These are missing optional startup files, not missing required menus or a first-snapshot blocker.

findings.name: No additional Ritual warning categories in the map sweep
findings.facts: Across the 66 default-verbosity startup logs there are no texture/shader/image, light-grid, animation or fatal-error diagnostics. F.A.K.K.2 has no warning lines. Known developer 1 mixed-image-registration, fraglimit/cheats and missing null.wav reports from the separate nine detailed runtime probes do not appear in this quieter map sweep.
findings.limits: Default verbosity and short first-snapshot dwell do not certify later content, all animation states or gameplay; detailed developer diagnostics remain recorded separately.

remainingGates: Complete campaign progression and collision gameplay remain open.
Renderer parity, broad animation-state coverage and muted-audio audition are not established by a map startup sweep.
ritual.unrelatedIssues: No additional Ritual blocker discovered in these 66 startup logs; detailed-probe warnings and OpenAL Soft capability limitations remain recorded in the runtime summary.

diagnostics.selectionRegex: WARNING|Warning|ERROR|error|Unknown|could not|Could not|failed|Failed|Bad init|does not exist|corrupted|not found|couldn.t exec

reconstructionReference.use: Reference observation only in this warning audit; no external implementation text incorporated.

classification.missing_images: BattleCry is absent from retail paks and documented. Other missing-image warnings appear in historical sweep; presence/absence is pinned under assetFacts. No current renderer crash from these fallbacks.
classification.patch_degeneracy: Known m4l3 twelve degenerate arches produce 48 reports; the prior patch harness reproduced the same 48 with OpenMoHAA, documented in the maps record.
classification.front_cull_token: Known shader-parser diagnostic with the same category/counts in the prior sweep. The parser leaves its current cull state unchanged; a zero-initialized shader defaults to CT_FRONT_SIDED. Explicit front recognition remains a parser cleanup possibility; this sweep establishes no new load blocker.
classification.light_grid_mismatch: credits and void only, also exactly two in the historical second sweep. Each retail map has six surfaces and a 768-byte palette but zero grid-offset/data bytes, pinned under lightGridFacts. The shared loader leaves lightGridData null on mismatch; no new campaign-map light-grid failure was observed.
classification.model_registration: Preexisting registration failures. 91 lines request files absent at their exact retail pak paths (88 player-model, two debris_255, one stieilhandgranate). Another 56 lines request vehicles/*.tik, whose exact paths are absent but corresponding models/vehicles/*.tik files exist. The same vehicle failures appear in the prior sweep. Preserve this path-form question as unresolved; absence at the requested path alone does not establish whether retail intended a prefix. The pinned reconstruction also passes the name unchanged to TIKI registration.
classification.sound_alias: Briefings and credits/void report footstep aliases excluded by the documented maps filter. The 108 SetCurrentTiki advisory lines describe possible errors rather than actual failed lookups.
classification.music_reference: m6l3b emits two aux1 command skips. Retail music/m6l3b.mus has two !aux1 commands and no aux1 song definition; musicFacts pins those lines and pak identity. The parser skips commands referencing an undefined song. No loss of another song or load failure is established.
classification.skeleton_boxes: Known in earlier multiplayer/campaign logs. The loader bounds-checks the box record and discards boxes while retaining the model. These warnings alone do not demonstrate animation or surface failure.
classification.invalid_event: The native cgame reports flickeralpha missing and one ClientGameCommandManager execution failure for welding_torch.tik. The same init-command warning appears in the prior Vulkan campaign log. This is a recurring module/content diagnostic; its visual effect has not been established.
classification.failed_event: Part of the welding_torch flickeralpha diagnostics, not a separate map-load failure.
classification.bad_init_command: Six avelocity, one flickeralpha and one cache init-command rejection; all named command/model pairs appear in prior logs. No new load failure is established, and their presentation effect remains unmeasured.
classification.bad_cache_command: One cache rejection for explosion_bridge.tik on m4l2, also present in the prior m4l2 log.
classification.startup_unknown_command: 54 fov diagnostics occur at startup before map loading. They are distinct from the native cgame reliable-command diagnostic. No current load failure or FOV effect is established.
classification.optional_config: 54 missing custom.cfg startup notices in isolated homes; no custom.cfg was supplied for this sweep.
classification.sound_parser_advisory: 108 boilerplate notices, two per map. They are not 108 actual SetCurrentTiki failures.
classification.unknown_client_command: NEWLY RECOGNIZED OPEN AUDIO CONTRACT: fadesound reaches native cgame without an engine interceptor. It also appears in historical valid campaign m3l1a and m5l3 logs. Runtime establishes unhandled delivery; intended fade and previous-map handling are reconstructed-source inferences recorded separately below.

newlyRecognizedOpenGaps: MOHAA reliable fadesound interception and fade lifecycle

observed.moduleAuthority: Retail gamex86.dll sender literals and native module delivery in fnTech3 logs; no retail engine execution.

fadeBoundary.sourceObserved: MOHAA import slot 118 drops differentServer and forwards the common command accessor; that accessor has no fadesound interceptor.
fadeBoundary.reconstructionInferred: Pinned OpenMoHAA consumes fadesound before native cgame, ignores it when differentServer is true, otherwise calls S_FadeSound(atof(argv[1])). Its snd_openal_new.cpp uses cls.realtime plus the positive duration (milliseconds); nonpositive duration cancels the fade and restores volume. This is reconstruction evidence, not a retail engine observation.

differentServer.effect: Not established by this sweep or the referenced reliable-command logs.

fadeBoundary.followup: Implement and test a MOHAA-owned audio fade preserving the shared spatial audio path; validate duration parsing, fade/update/cancel/shutdown lifecycle and previous-map behavior with other-profile controls.

unrelatedStaticFinding.fact: TIKI_FindTikiAnim passes an uninitialized filename array to tikianimcache->find; unlike TIKI_FindTiki it does not copy/canonicalize path first.
unrelatedStaticFinding.provenance: Inherited unchanged from the pinned OpenMoHAA code/tiki/tiki_cache.cpp:58.
unrelatedStaticFinding.status: No change during the frozen suite; no runtime effect established.
